correctness.rationale: By marking the event f(i)=j,f(j)=i, each unhit vertex other than i,j has conditional unhit probability (1-p_v)^(n-2). Summing pairs and subtracting E[Z]E[T] yields exactly ((1+s2)V-2s2W)/2. For P taking value p_i with mass p_i and decreasing h=(1-P)^(n-2), the independent-copy identity gives V<=s2W, strict unless n=2 or P constant. With two positive p_i, 0<s2<1 and W>0; hence strict negative covariance and exact equality classification. Separately, conditioned on any vertex unhit, normalized target probabilities make expected fixed-point count equal one, proving orthogonality. Exact fractional enumeration of 150456 maps and 318 assertions independently checked finite instances. No dependence on computation for the infinite real-p theorem.

originality.rationale: The claim is a strict covariance sign with explicit lower-magnitude bound for every heterogeneous common-target probability vector and a complete equality case. Finch 2022 treats uniform random functions and cycle-length statistics; Hansen–Jaworski 2008 treats exchangeable indegrees, which nonuniform p normally violates. Closest accessible preexisting uniform source/cycle and fixedpoint/indegree statements are strict special cases and do not imply a heterogeneous all-p bound. Genuine searches of result records, published corpus and primary literature found no theorem establishing that inequality for all p. Earlier general p-mapping calculus might yield it implicitly; lack of a match alone is not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Historical p-mapping occupancy and factorial-moment methods may yield the sign inequality implicitly even if not stated with these words.
The 2008 local-properties companion article was compared at abstract level only; cannot assert complete noncoverage of its body.
Semantic mathematical-result searches and literature searches are not exhaustive; independent novelty validation is not performed.

value.rationale: Sources (indegree-zero vertices) and directed 2-cycles are natural complementary structural observables of functional graphs. The sharp all-vector covariance bound survives arbitrary weighted target heterogeneity, including zero weights, and equality precisely characterizes flat positive weights; the one-cycle contrast identifies a structural boundary. It concerns an entire probabilistic family and gives a quantitative sign law rather than a selected finite parameter computation. Its proof uses an antitone inequality but the motivated graph-statistic synthesis and sharp classification are substantive.
